evidence.finding: Candidate kernel (Block Dim 1024, Task Duration 255453 us) per-block mean aiv_time 9824.9 us with min 9787.1 / max 9847.1 across all 1024 blocks: every program executes identical work and per-block time is uniform. Per block only ~32 KB of output is produced (128 serial iterations x 256 B), yet aiv_mte3_instructions=8193 (8192 per block, ~128 B per instruction) and write_main_memory_datas=1024 KB per block (32x the bytes the program actually has to write), while aiv_main_mem_write_bw is only 0.099 GB/s per block and read BW ~0.008 GB/s (sum over blocks ~8 GB/s). Pipe use: aiv_vec_ratio 0.5387, mte2_ratio 0.0010, mte3_ratio 0.1038, vec_wait_ratio 0.1510. So the cost is instruction/memory-op fragmentation at tiny granularity, not HBM/L2 bandwidth.

Compiled with BLOCK_X=128, BLOCK_Y=1 for the target case. Program maps only over spatial output; all N*C planes are handled by nested scf.for loops (128 serial iterations). Output row/column indices are produced by arith.remsi (`(pid_x*BLOCK_X+arange) % OW`), so the store offsets are a 2-D tensor<1x128> whose contiguity/alignment the compiler cannot prove; the IR keeps tensor<1x128> pointer arithmetic with mixed i32/i64 and the store is emitted from that wrapped index tensor.

Target case upsample_bilinear2d-timing-1: 253.949 ms vs reference 0.2455 ms (speedup 0.00097x); timing-0/2/4 are ~8.6-9.9 ms and timing-3/5 ~256-294 ms. 6 of 24 formal cases fail with MLIRCompilationError in ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR (correctness-2,3,8,9,14,15), i.e. part of the contract does not even compile.

All 16 tuned configs keep BLOCK_X in {64..512} and BLOCK_Y in {1,2} with num_warps 4/8: the supplied tuning space never expresses a full-output-row tile, so the retile mechanism I test is outside the supplied search space rather than a repetition of it.

record.hypothesis: The 254 ms on the target case is set by per-program instruction count, not by occupancy or bandwidth: the kernel writes its 128-element row chunk through a `% OW`-wrapped, shape-[1,128] index tensor, so Triton-Ascend emits ~8192 tiny mte3 stores (and ~8192 mte2 loads) per program with ~128 B granularity and ~32x write amplification, and every program additionally replays a 128-iteration serial N*C loop over that fragmented index pattern. Retiling to (plane, row-block, column-block) with explicit block indices plus a bounds mask instead of modular wrap should let the compiler prove the full-width row store is contiguous/aligned and emit a few wide DMAs instead of thousands of tiny ones.
record.change: Single mechanism: retile programs. Replace the spatial-only grid + `% OW`/`% OH` index wrap + serial N*C loop with a 3-D grid (column block, row block, plane = n*C+c), full-width row tiles whose column index is `pid*BLOCK_W + arange` plus an explicit `ow < OW`/`oh < OH` mask, and 2-D [BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W] weights/taps computed from the same formulas. Per-element math (fp32 coordinate mapping, clamping, 2-D bilinear weights, fp32 accumulation order) is kept identical. Compatibility edits (recorded separately from performance): (a) move the align_corners ratio (IH-1)/(OH-1) computation to the host in Python and feed it as a float kernel argument so no integer division appears in the kernel (the align_corners branch currently fails ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR on 6 formal cases); (b) add the required public entrypoint alias `run(input, output_size, align_corners=False, scales_h=None, scales_w=None)` next to the preserved FlagGems `upsample_bilinear2d`. No caching, no host-side computation of tensor values.
record.expected: If the diagnosis holds, the candidate kernel's mte3 instruction count per program drops from thousands to a handful of wide stores and the 32x write amplification disappears; target-case full-call time should drop by at least an order of magnitude from 253.95 ms (expected tens of ms or below), with the target still correct. The 6 previously non-compiling align_corners cases should start running. Gather loads (4 taps per output element) remain and are expected to become the next visible limit; if time stays near 254 ms and per-block mte3 counts stay ~8000, this mechanism is falsified.
record.validation: Preflight: source review + compile of the edited candidate. Then the host formal evaluation over the 24 formal cases plus supplementary and CANN supplementary checks; compare per-case latency and pass count with baseline-evaluation.json, and confirm the align_corners cases now compile and match within atol/rtol 0.015 at required_matched_ratio 1.0. No re-collected paired profiling is available from this call, so the mte3-instruction prediction stays an expectation, not a measurement.
alternatives: The kernel is HBM/L2-bandwidth-bound: contradicted by aiv_main_mem_write_bw 0.099 GB/s and aiv_main_mem_read_bw 0.008 GB/s per block (sum ~100 and ~8 GB/s), far below device capability, and by mte2_ratio 0.0010.

The serial N*C loop starves parallelism: contradicted by uniform per-block aiv_time (min 9787 us, max 9847 us) over 1024 blocks; the machine is already fully occupied and total time is waves x per-program time, so only per-program work/instruction count can reduce the total.

record.hypothesis: For the target case (FP16 [4,32,128,128] -> [4,32,256,256], align_corners=False, exact scale 2) the current exact-2x fast path is bound by per-program fixed cost, not by arithmetic or DRAM traffic: 16384 programs each move only ~9 x 256B and pay a mask/select sequence per load. If each program instead covers a tile of ROWS=8 input rows x the full 128-wide row with unmasked, address-clamped loads and clamped edges, the program count drops 8x (16384 -> 2048), every load becomes one contiguous 2KB transfer, and the per-load MOVEMASK/MOVEV/VSEL fix-ups disappear because the address clamp already yields the edge sample.
record.change: Performance change (one mechanism: amortize per-program fixed cost in the exact-2x fast path): rewrite upsample_bilinear2d_2x_kernel to a row-tiled kernel, grid (cdiv(IW,BLOCK_J), cdiv(IH,ROWS), N*C) with ROWS=8, BLOCK_J=128, 2-D (ROWS,BLOCK_J) tiles, 9 loads per program instead of 9 per 2 output rows; replace masked loads plus tl.where edge fix-ups by address clamping (maximum/minimum on the index vectors), which is exactly PyTorch's edge clamp; keep the constant 0.25/0.75 separable weights, the fp32 accumulation and the (ROWS,BLOCK_J,2) interleaved contiguous store pattern; keep a mask on the store only when IH % ROWS or IW % BLOCK_J is non-zero. Compatibility edits (recorded separately, no performance claim): (a) remove @triton.autotune and the copied FlagGems config list from the generic kernel and launch it with one fixed constexpr config (BLOCK_X=256, BLOCK_Y=2) so no do_bench/clear_cache path is reachable; (b) expose a single public symbol `run` and make the FlagGems-named implementation and helpers private (_upsample_bilinear2d, _device_context, _bilinear_reciprocal_scale) so no conflicting public symbol exists.
record.expected: Target case: program count 16384 -> 2048, MTE2 instruction total ~8x lower, contiguous 2KB loads instead of 256B loads, no mask/select instructions on the load path; expect device Task Duration to drop well below 55450.8us (conservative expectation >= 2x better, i.e. < 27ms) with identical outputs. Generic (non-2x) path: numerically unchanged, only the tuning constant changes.
record.validation: Host preflight over the 24 formal cases plus supplementary checks (correctness of the exact-2x path against the frozen contract: even output row 2i = 0.25*x[i-1]+0.75*x[i], odd row 2i+1 = 0.75*x[i]+0.25*x[i+1], edge rows degenerate to the clamped sample; generic path is bit-identical code except the fixed BLOCK constants), then full performance on upsample_bilinear2d-timing-1; check that block count and total task duration move in the predicted direction before claiming a mechanism.
alternatives: Keep the grid unchanged and only remove the masks (address-clamped loads): removes select instructions but keeps 16384 programs and 256B transfers, so the per-program amortization is not addressed.

Keep the kernel and only raise BLOCK_J / process several (n,c) planes per program in a serial loop: reduces program count without enlarging the DMA transfer, and the native tuned space already shows BLOCK_X<=512 does not help.
Switch the interpolation math to fp16 to halve vector work: plausible later, but the reference computes in fp32 and this does not touch the dominant per-program overhead.
Write a fully data-dependent (generic) kernel for the 2x case: reintroduces per-lane coordinate arithmetic the fixed-weight path avoids.
record.discriminating_observation: If per-program fixed cost dominates, cutting the program count 8x while keeping identical arithmetic must cut the device Task Duration far below the measured 55450.8us and cut the total MTE2 instruction count by roughly 8x (344064 -> ~43000) with per-block mean times only growing sub-linearly; vector FLOPs per output element stay unchanged. If instead the case were bound by vector arithmetic volume or DRAM bandwidth, the same edit would leave the duration nearly unchanged.

review_feedback.finding: In exact2x path, jl=max(j-1,0) has no upper bound. For width tails (for example IW=3, BLOCK_J=128), inactive lanes still perform unmasked loads. On final nc and final input row those addresses can exceed the allocated input even though output stores are masked. Passing existing cases cannot prove those reads safe. Repair address bounds or load masking in the model-generated candidate before retention. No performance strategy provided.

evidence.finding: Untouched native kernel fails verification at the store line: tl.store(ptr_o + offset_o, result) stores an fp32 expression into a pointer whose element type is the output dtype. TritonToStructuredIncubated/Canonicalizer pipeline aborts, so the native source cannot compile for Ascend as-is.

Kernel computes the bilinear result in tl.float32 and stores without casting to the output element type. It also imports FlagGems-only runtime helpers (runtime.get_tuned_config, runtime.device.name, torch_device_fn.device, triton_lang_extension.program_id) and exposes only upsample_bilinear2d, not the contract's run entrypoint.

Contract requires public run(input, output_size, align_corners=False, scales_h=None, scales_w=None) returning out, with no mutation or aliasing; output dtype/device follow input. Semantic algorithm must be preserved.

Shared compatibility phase: make the unmodified FlagGems algorithm compile and satisfy the contract, no performance optimization, preserve source ancestry and launch geometry; maximum 2 generation calls, formal evaluation pending.

record.hypothesis: The compilation failure is a dtype mismatch at the store: the 2x2 bilinear accumulation is fp32 while output buffers may be fp16/bf16. Casting the result to ptr_o.dtype.element_ty should satisfy tt.store's value/pointer type rule without changing the interpolation math. Separately, FlagGems-only module metadata (tuned configs, device-name assert, device context, tle.program_id) must be replaced by plain Triton/host equivalents so the module imports and exposes run.
record.change: Keep the kernel algorithm, loop structure, interpolation formula, 2D grid geometry (BLOCK_X over OW, BLOCK_Y over OH) and autotune key unchanged. Minimal edits: (1) tl.store(ptr_o + offset_o, result.to(ptr_o.dtype.element_ty)); (2) replace tle.program_id with tl.program_id; (3) replace runtime.get_tuned_config with a local single triton.Config list for BLOCK_X/BLOCK_Y; (4) drop the FlagGems device-name assert and torch_device_fn.device context, using torch.empty on input.device and a plain kernel launch; (5) expose run as the public entrypoint while keeping the original function name as an alias.
record.expected: Candidate imports without FlagGems dependencies and compiles under Triton-Ascend: no tt.store verifier error, one kernel program per (BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y) output tile, and numerically identical results to the preserved fp32 accumulation (cast only at store). No performance change is claimed or targeted.

alternatives: Pass an explicit OUT_DTYPE constexpr and cast result accordingly; rejected as more invasive than reading ptr_o.dtype.element_ty.
Compute the accumulation in the output dtype; rejected because it changes numerical behavior of the preserved formula.
Replace autotune entirely with hardcoded launch meta; rejected as a larger structural change than a local one-config equivalent of get_tuned_config.
